key_insight: A small set of human visual style cues can drive a large share of the social biases shown by multimodal large language models. StylisticBias isolates appearance from identity, revealing which facial attributes most influence biased judgments.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of measuring social bias in MLLMs when studies compare different people, making it hard to tell whether the model is reacting to identity, appearance, or both. It provides a controlled benchmark for attribute-level bias analysis.
method: Created StylisticBias, a benchmark using 500 photorealistic base faces to control for identity while varying specific visual attributes.
Evaluated MLLMs on attribute-level social judgments to identify which stylistic cues trigger biased responses.
Compared model behavior across controlled face variations to separate appearance effects from person-specific differences.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a more precise way to audit and debug social bias in multimodal systems. It can improve model evaluation, inform safer deployment, and guide bias mitigation focused on the specific visual cues that matter most.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing base face generation and controlled attribute edits
Side-by-side face grid highlighting one attribute change at a time
Bar chart ranking visual cues by bias strength
Simple icon set for fairness, face attributes, and MLLM evaluation
paper_title: StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs
paper_authors: Shaghayegh Kolli, Timo Cavelius, Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Samantha Dalal, Jana Diesner
